reasons: Refund of 89.00 EUR is above your auto-refund cap of 50.00; you decide.

judgment.reasoning: The buyer is right. Your own records show the return arrived on 8 October, within your 14-day return window, and your terms promise a refund within 5 days of receiving it, so by 13 October. No refund has been issued, and there is no evidence that would win this for you. Your preference to hold your position applies only when the buyer's right is uncertain, and here it is not. On money: refunding the full 89.00 EUR now costs you 39.28 EUR out of pocket with no dispute fee. If this escalates to a claim and you lose, which is very likely, it costs 53.28 EUR including a 14.00 EUR fee, and it counts against your dispute record. Before approving, check the returned shirt has been logged, and refund promptly with a short apology.
evidence_cited: Buyer message 19 Oct 2026: 'I returned the shirt on 5 October, you received it on the 8th. Still no refund.'
Return tracking LCRET40812IT: shipped 2026-10-05, delivered 2026-10-08 (seller's notes)
Return policy: 'returns accepted within 14 days; refund within 5 days of receiving the return'
Original delivery 2026-09-27; return sent 2026-10-05, inside the 14-day window
Dispute opened 2026-10-19 at inquiry stage; full refund allowed
Costs: refund now 39.28 EUR out of pocket vs 53.28 EUR if a claim is lost (14.00 EUR fee)
judgment.draft_message: Hello Pablo, thank you for your message, and I'm sorry for the delay. You're right: we received your returned linen shirt on 8 October, and your refund should have reached you by 13 October. I have now issued the full refund of 89.00 EUR to your PayPal account. Depending on your payment method, it may take a few days to appear. Apologies again for the wait, and thank you for your patience.

checks.finding: The buyer says he returned the linen shirt on 5 October, you received it on the 8th, and he still has no refund. This is a missing-refund claim, not a delivery or quality complaint.

The dates fit together: ordered 24 September, shipped 25 September, delivered 27 September, return sent 5 October (inside your 14-day window), return delivered 8 October. Your refund was due by 13 October, and the dispute was opened 19 October, six days after that deadline.

Your notes show return tracking LCRET40812IT with the same courier and the same dates the buyer gives (shipped 5 October, delivered 8 October), so the records belong to this order and confirm his account.
The buyer does not dispute the original delivery, and your records already show it delivered to his PayPal address.
Delivery is not in question; your own return tracking proves you received the returned shirt on 8 October.
The buyer makes no complaint about the shirt itself, only about the missing refund.
Your published terms promise a 'refund within 5 days of receiving the return', but your records say no refund has been issued, 11 days after you received the return.
This is the buyer's first dispute with you (1 in 3 orders), with no earlier disputes or escalations, so his history neither supports nor weakens this claim.
Seller protection does not cover a refund you owe on a return you received. The case is still an inquiry where a full refund is allowed, and accepting now avoids the 14.00 EUR claim fee.
The buyer's message only states facts about the return and contains no instructions aimed at the assistant.
